decision.summaryForCoordinator: The test that settled the five sibling input corpora fails here, and reading that failure correctly is the whole review. Only 1 of 22 states is a whole-sentence live substring; a mechanical substring check would report 21 defects and all 21 would be wrong. This artifact COMPOSES states from live fragments, because the live text offers nothing per-platform or per-delta to lift — exactByteIntent says 'Per platform: the four published deltas bound to pairedWorkload inputs…', with the four delta names in measures and passProperty and the platform axis in matrix. So I verified at fragment level instead: all sixteen distinct fragments resolve to live harness fields, with none invented. What made that checkable is the artifact's own practice — the sixteen per-platform source fields put the lifted text in single quote marks and then append two live sentences verbatim, so quotation is separated from composition rather than blurred. The 'cap' prohibition is the second thing counting cannot settle: the word occurs 43 times, the highest prohibited-token count in this sequence, and every occurrence is a refusal or live text. The decisive test is whether a cap value exists, and the complete standalone-integer set is 1 and 26. The live specification repeats the point four ways — threshold.bound 'NO numeric cap in D-006', passProperty 'Caps are not applied', doesNotClaim 'Does not invent caps', and register cell [6] 'caps deferred by explicit disposition'. That left 21 as the only substantive number, which needed classifying rather than sweeping: it appears only inside the live compound tokens '21-pair' and 'N=21' and is a matched-pair sample size, not a threshold anything can exceed. On the workload prohibition, live failsIf makes 'start or RSS uses analyze or a consented probe as the workload' a failure, and the subject's command state carries the live exclusion as an exact substring — 'Not analyze. Not a consented doctor probe.' — with every other mention a refusal. The version question repeats the G02 pattern: three harness files with byte-identical harness objects, all three naming v1 as artifactPathWhenAuthored, v1 and v3 sharing the accepted parent. Citing v1 is correct and the subject names that justification. All three cited digests match, all 22 fixtureBytes read NOT-AUTHORED with no measured value, delta or median anywhere in initialStates, the class member phrase equals live claimVerbatim on all 22 states and the live register cell [1], and the subject did not move. Twenty-seven attacks run, twenty-seven refuted, zero findings. One item for a successor rather than a defect: the exact-bytes state composes three live fragments but its source names two of the three origins, omitting pairedWorkload.n — which is nonetheless cited by name on the neighbouring state, and all three fragments are live and exact.
